transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Patel, thank you for coming back in to see me today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is this about the biopsy results? I've been staring at my phone for three days.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is. I need to share some very difficult news with you. There was a serious error in the pathology lab. Your specimen was mislabelled, and the diagnosis of cancer you were given actually belongs to another patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. What?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry. We failed to ensure the correct labels were on your samples, and as a result, you were given the wrong information.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are telling me that I don't have cancer? Or that you don't know if I have it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We do not know the status of your specific biopsy right now because the sample was compromised. We need to repeat the procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. I have spent seventy-two hours thinking my life was over. I've already started looking at leave policies for my job. How does a label just get swapped?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a heavy thing to process, and I can see how distressing this is.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Distressing? That is an understatement. I knew I shouldn't have come to this clinic. I told myself the paperwork looked sloppy when I signed in.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do you even know who is responsible for this? Was it the person taking the sample or the person in the lab?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The team and I take full responsibility for this mistake. It was our failure in the chain of custody.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Responsibility doesn't exactly fix the last three days. My head is spinning. I feel like I'm being lied to, or just managed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize how jarring it is to have the ground shift like this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens now? Do I just trust you to do it again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will need to schedule a new biopsy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? And how do I know the second one won't end up belonging to someone else?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will look into the scheduling. We will see what we can do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a date. I need a date.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a specific day right this second, but we'll get it sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is exactly why I read every single line of every form I sign. Because the people actually doing the work aren't paying attention. Who is reviewing this? Is there a supervisor?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop saying you understand. You don't know what it's like to be told you have a malignant tumor and then be told it was a clerical error.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't imagine the toll those three days took on you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want a written record of this. I want to know exactly how the mislabelling happened. Not just "it happened," but the step-by-step failure.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can look into providing a summary.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A summary isn't a record. I want the actual lab log.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have to check if that's possible.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why is it not possible? If you can mislabel a human organ, you can certainly print out a log.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will see what can be done.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not leaving until I have a plan. You said we need to repeat the procedure. When? Where? Who is doing it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will get you back on the schedule soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: "Soon" is not a clinical plan. I am a software engineer; I deal with logic and timelines. Give me a timeline.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will check the surgical schedule and we will send you an email.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And if I don't get the email?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You'll get the email.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't trust your emails. I don't trust this process.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is an incredibly difficult moment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's a disaster.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is there anyone else I can talk to? A patient advocate?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can find out who that is.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are the doctor. Why don't you know who the advocate is?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will check the directory.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is an absolute joke.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient and remains regulated and calm despite significant pushback and hostility.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the first turn, but the resident never performed a comprehension check.

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language and explicitly stated the team takes full responsibility without deflection.

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions ('distressing', 'jarring') and engaged with the patient's distress, though some responses were generic.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders ('get it sorted', 'soon', 'will check') and failed to provide a specific timeline or date.
